labels.label: erslem:PropertyTimelike
labels.notes: Reported partial and unmarked. That is right: three of its readings are not of record. I read the Lean against ghd_02_19.tex:1143-1151 (the statement), :1102-1105 ((4.83)) and :814 (GHD). The elaborated signature of ers_lemma_4_86 is {E} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] {δ} (hδ : 0 < δ) {C : Causality (ℝ × E)} {U₁ : Opens (ℝ × E)} {S}, CurveNestedOn (slopeCone E δ hδ) C U₁ ∨ CurveNestedOn (slopeCone E δ hδ) C.dual U₁ → C.IsCauchySurfaceOn U₁ S → (∀ q ∈ S, q.1 = 0) → BoundaryGraph U₁ (closure S). Each weakening the REPORT claims is real. (1) No GloballyHyperbolicOn is asked. hS is IsCauchySurfaceOn (DEC-14, exactly once), and the proof uses only existence: IsCauchySurfaceOn.exists_mem_connectedComponentIn throws away the uniqueness half of ∃!. (2) S is assumed only ⊆ {t = 0}. Openness, connectedness and S ⊆ U₁ are not assumed. S ⊆ U₁ enters only ers_lemma_4_86_edge, and the paper's GHD definition (:814) has it. (3) E is any real normed space. (4) The ℓ¹ instance elaborates: a probe applied ers_lemma_4_86 and ers_lemma_4_86_oneSidedBoundary to E = WithLp 1 (Fin d → ℝ) and checked ‖v‖ = Σ‖v i‖ (PiLp.norm_eq_of_L1). The readings are disclosed. (a) (4.87) is read as the closed slope-δ′ cone, δ′ < δ, curve-nested in C on U₁. That is the binder's note on erslem:PropertyTimelike, binder.toml:424. The disjunction C / C.dual is ':1160 without loss of generality'. It suffices because the paper's U₁ is connected: every point lies on an inextendible curve through the connected S, and ∂₀ is timelike throughout. (b) (4.83) is read in the identity chart over a cylinder, with flipT below {t = 0}. Below the graph, z ∈ U ↔ z.1 < f z.2; on it, frontier U ↔ z.1 = f z.2; and f maps into (t₀−ε, t₀+ε). That is the paper's below/graph/above trichotomy. The cube chart follows by an elementary step that is not formalised: for E = Fin d → ℝ (sup norm, with (4.87) giving a slope < δ/d), a rescaling of space; for E = ℓ¹, a shrink to an inscribed cube first. (c) The Lorentzian Cauchy hypersurface is read as ETT's (DEC-14), applied to ERS, which is the binder's standing reading. (d) ∂S is closure S, shown immaterial when S ⊆ U₁: frontier_diff_closure_eq_frontier_diff_edge is correct, since U₁ is open and S ∩ frontier U₁ = ∅. The edge form is ers_lemma_4_86_edge. But see the finding on how OQ-41 (e) is cited. It is not vacuous: minkowskiSlab_ers_lemma_4_86 satisfies every hypothesis and has a non-empty ∂U₁ ∖ closure S. The label is written without ** (QuasilinearOneSided.lean:16).

labels.label: T-loc-quasilinear-one-sided/1-one-sided
labels.notes: The target's title (roadmap.toml:989) asks for four things: the slope-δ static cone curve-nested in C_g; U₁ C_g-GH with S open in {x⁰ = 0}; ∂U₁ ∖ ∂S locally a continuous graph with U₁ below; hence OneSidedBoundary U₁ (closure S). ers_lemma_4_86 and ers_lemma_4_86_oneSidedBoundary prove this with weaker hypotheses, and nothing is narrowed. Nesting on U₁ is weaker than at M (CurveNestedOn.mono), and the C.dual disjunct only widens. GH and openness are dropped. The flipT chart is a chart, so 'U₁ below' holds in it. The library's definitions are used exactly. CurveNestedOn is Causal.Causality.CurveNestedOn, the ladder's curve_nested (ladder.toml:364). OneSidedAt and OneSidedBoundary are LadderLocal.lean:181/190, proved by unfolding: LiesBelowGraphAt.oneSidedAt does intro N hN and gives the V with V ∩ U preconnected as an image of ball × (0,1). slopeCone E δ hδ is staticCausality E transported along (t,x) ↦ (t, δx). slopeCone_le_top_iff proves ≤ ⟺ ‖q.2 − p.2‖ ≤ δ(q.1 − p.1), the closed cone of slope δ around ∂₀. Its causal curves are the δ-Lipschitz graphs (slopeCone_causalCurveOn_graph), the static cone the binder means. The target's evidence reads ∂S as closure(S) ∖ S (OQ-41 (e)). In that reading the target's statement is ers_lemma_4_86_edge, which the same module proves under S ⊆ U₁, part of 'Cauchy surface of U₁'. The sub-label's decl list omits it (finding 1).

labels.label: T-loc-quasilinear-one-sided/3-inextensible-piece
labels.notes: Signature: {M} [TopologicalSpace M] {C : Causality M} [T2Space M] {W} {ℓ}, Continuous ℓ → ∀ {T}, Continuous T → (∀ τ, T (ℓ τ) = τ) → (∀ a b, a ≤ b → (∀ τ ∈ Icc a b, ℓ τ ∈ W) → C.CausalCurveOn W ℓ a b) → ∀ {t}, ℓ t ∈ W → C.Inextensible W (connectedComponentIn (ℓ ⁻¹' W) t) ℓ. It is true and kernel-checked. Its only class hypothesis beyond the topology is T2, as claimed, and T2 is needed: tendsto_nhds_unique at a finite end. On the line with two origins, with W the complement of one origin, the piece (0, ∞) extends through the other origin. The continuous time T and the segment hypothesis are ordinary hypotheses, not standing. No CurvesExtend, no axiom of C beyond the curve API, nothing outside W. Hoist check for kb/0047: section 2, copied verbatim under only `import Causal.Inextensible`, `Causal.Cauchy`, `Causal.LadderLocal`, elaborates with -DwarningAsError=true. Those modules' import closure is 27 modules, with no Static, Minkowski, Flat.*, Model.*, Port.* or CBG.*. With Inextensible and Cauchy alone it fails only on the Mathlib instance LocallyConnectedSpace ℝ, which LadderLocal's imports supply. So nothing model-layer is used, and the lemma can be hoisted to the ETT layer. Its companions futureInextensible_of_isLUB_notMem, pastInextensible_of_isGLB_notMem and IsCauchySurfaceOn.exists_mem_connectedComponentIn are in the same section and hoist with it.

build.details: Build: cd lean-causal && taskset -c 0-11 lake env lean -DwarningAsError=true scaffold/CausalScaffold/QuasilinearOneSided.lean gives exit 0 and no output. grep finds no sorry, admit, axiom, native_decide, unsafe, opaque, extern or set_option. #print axioms: the probe was a verbatim copy of the file plus #print axioms of all 36 declared names, under the campaign directory, deleted. Each gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], including the 13 the REPORT names. The 36 names are exactly the REPORT's decls ∪ extra_decls. Probes: the ℓ¹ instance (above). Section 2 under ETT imports only (above). The file without Causal.Flat.LipschitzGraph, sections 1-7 (above). Imports: the direct imports are the five claimed. Walking the import lines, the transitive Causal closure is 38 modules: 32 from the first four, plus Minkowski, Flat.Form, Flat.Achronal, Flat.Cosmological, Flat.Penrose and Flat.LipschitzGraph from the fifth. None is Causal.Port.*, Causal.Model.* or Causal.CBG.*. Name clashes: the file body elaborates under `import Causal`, which imports all 242 strict modules, with -DwarningAsError=true and no error. A sanity probe confirmed that a duplicate name is reported. A grep of every declaration keyword in Causal/** (FlatTimeCylinder included, read-only) and scaffold/** (RationalLineExtras included, read-only) finds none of the 36 short names. Graduation to Causal/Model/QuasilinearOneSided.lean is a file move with no clash. for_keeper: simulated on a copy of programme/ladder.toml, `tools/ladder.py check --file` reports only that Causal.ers_lemma_4_86_oneSidedBoundary is not yet in lean-causal/Causal. That resolves after graduation. Its keys at, statement, witness, under and status fit the [[consequence]] schema, and note is for_keeper commentary as in the other REPORTs. Paper findings, checked against ghd_02_19.tex. (1) :1160 is true as stated. 't₀ ≠ 0' is not a topological consequence of p ∉ ∂S: a diffeomorphic distortion of a 1+1 domain of dependence can touch {x⁰ = 0} outside closure S. It follows here from (4.87) plus the Cauchy property, via the vertical projections (proj_mem_of_curveNestedOn, the t₀ = 0 case of ers_lemma_4_86_future). (2) :1162 and its footnote: an accurate account of the formalisation, not a claimed error of the paper. ETT's Cauchy surface is met by two-sided inextensible curves (DEC-11, DEC-13, DEC-14), and the library has no extension principle for an abstract C. The whole-line piece meets S at time 0, which makes the footnote's case distinction unnecessary. (3) :1168, f⁺ is 1/δ-Lipschitz: true. The past cone gives f⁺(y′) ≥ f⁺(y) − ‖y − y′‖/δ, and symmetrically. exists_lipschitz_graph_of_cone proves it on a ball, for its F, which equals ERS's f⁺ there by downward closure of the fibres. (4) :1168 typo: '(x⁰, f⁺(x)) ∉ U₁' is ill-typed, and the intended '(x⁰, x) ∉ U₁ for x⁰ ≥ f⁺(x)' holds globally, because the cone makes each fibre above {x⁰ = 0} the interval [0, f⁺(x)). That theorem assumes C.IsCauchySurfaceOn U₁ S, which is ∃! (exactly once).
